description: Raise n=1024 panel OCCUPANCY past 1 CTA/SM by tail-streaming the panel instead of caching all m rows in SMEM. A sibling profiled n=1024 as GPU-bound ~90% but stuck at 1 CTA/SM because the single-CTA panel keeps the FULL m=1024-row column resident in SMEM (~131KB/CTA → only 1 block/SM, the occupancy wall). Restructure the panel kernel to keep ONLY the active NB-wide sub-panel rows (or a fixed window) in SMEM and STREAM the tail rows from global memory per Householder column (cp.async double-buffer the row tiles), dropping SMEM/CTA below ~64KB so 2-3 CTAs/SM fit. More resident CTAs = the idle-SM occupancy the n=1024 B=60 shape (60 matrices/148 SMs) is starved for. This is distinct from raw nb-widening (which conserves work) — it attacks occupancy directly. FP32 panel. Keep n!=1024 as parent. Use the reusable ldv!=cb artifact from brief 31 if helpful. Avoid the substring 'stream' incl. comments (use 'pipe'/'feed in chunks'); single default queue; stock libs only.

Windowed n=1024 panel: cb=32 cols in a global col-major scratch Pg(B,nb,n); CTA keeps a WROWS=128-row double-buffered window in SMEM, pipes the m=1024 rows in chunks via cp.async (3 passes/col: scale, w_c dots, update+fused-next-norm); unblocked Householder identical reflectors/tau/R/V/T to panel_factor_kernel. threads=128. n=1024 ONLY (use_win=(n==1024)); n!=1024 byte-identical to parent. SMEM/CTA 139KB->~38KB (Block-Limit-SMEM 1->4). Validation PASS (22 tests + diff_correctness + invariance + offgrid + kernelguard CLEAN). Benchmark under ~1.5x contention geomean 17003us (parent 9032 same env). n=1024 dense shape4 85894-92181us vs parent 21009 (~4.4x slower); contention-invariant shape4/shape3 ratio 3.465 (parent 1.189). nsys contention-immune: windowed kernel 53.3ms vs parent resident 11.5ms (4.6x). ncu: kernel is LATENCY-bound (issue every 5.3cyc, 3.96 warps/SM, 0.10 waves/SM, compute 7.5% mem 7.1% DRAM 0.08%), NOT SMEM-bound -- the SMEM drop is wasted because at B=60 there are only 60 CTAs for 148 SMs.

Widen windowed n=1024 CTA to 512 threads (16 warps, vs 128) + WROWS 128->256, to expose more eligible warps to hide the fixed-latency serial-chain stalls ncu flagged, and cut chunk/sync count. Validation PASS (all tests+guards+kernelguard CLEAN). Benchmark under contention geomean 16768us (trial1 17003). n=1024 shape4 85894us, contention-invariant shape4/shape3 ratio 3.229 (trial1 3.465, parent 1.189). nsys contention-immune windowed kernel 49.4ms (trial1 53.3ms; parent 11.5ms): the wider CTA bought ~7% kernel-time but still 4.3x slower than resident. Confirms single-CTA-per-matrix windowing cannot fill 148 SMs at B=60 regardless of SMEM/threads (CTA-count starvation, not per-CTA occupancy).

Cut windowed n=1024 panel 3->2 passes/column: scale col k ON READ in the w_c/update sweeps (v[r]=raw/denom) and write the scaled reflector back inside the update pass, eliminating the separate scale write-sweep + its syncs. threads=512, WROWS=256. Validation PASS (all tests+guards+kernelguard CLEAN); n=1024 residuals bit-match trial2. Benchmark under contention geomean 16690us (trial2 16769). n=1024 shape4 85268us, contention-invariant shape4/shape3 ratio 3.205 (trial2 3.229, parent 1.189). nsys contention-immune windowed kernel 51.4ms (within run noise of trial2 49.4ms; parent 11.5ms). Halving passes gave only marginal gain -> the limiter is the serial cb-deep Householder chain + 0.10-wave CTA starvation, not pass count. Best windowed geomean 16690us is a ~1.85x REGRESSION vs parent (contention-adjusted ~4.3x on n=1024 alone).

Built and measured the brief's tail-feed windowed n=1024 panel across 3 validated trials (all 22 tests + diff_correctness + invariance + offgrid + kernelguard CLEAN; n!=1024 byte-identical to parent). The SMEM-drop the brief targeted WORKS as designed -- cb cols moved to a global col-major scratch, CTA keeps only a WROWS-row cp.async double-buffered window, SMEM/CTA 139KB->~38KB, ncu Block-Limit-SMEM 1->4. But it does NOT translate to a win: best windowed geomean 16690us is a regression vs parent 9032us (contention-immune nsys: windowed kernel 49-53ms vs parent RESIDENT panel 11.5ms on n=1024 dense, ~4.3-4.6x slower across all 3 trials). Contention-invariant shape4(n1024)/shape3(n512) ratio held 3.2-3.5 vs parent 1.189.

ROOT CAUSE (ncu, contention-immune): the windowed kernel is LATENCY-bound, not SMEM-bound -- issue every 5.3 cyc, only 3.96 active warps/SM, achieved occupancy 6%, **Waves Per SM = 0.10**, compute 7.5% / mem 7.1% / DRAM 0.08%. At B=60 there are only 60 CTAs for 148 SMs, so 1 CTA/matrix uses at most 60 SMs no matter how many CTAs/SM the SMEM allows -- the brief's causal chain 'drop SMEM -> 2-3 CTAs/SM -> fill idle SMs' breaks at the last arrow because CTA_count(60) < SM_count(148). Dropping SMEM gives free CTA/SM slots that cannot be filled. The extra global re-reads + chunk syncs add serial-chain latency the resident SMEM panel avoids, so windowing strictly loses here. Widening the CTA 128->512 (+7% kernel time) and cutting 3->2 passes/col (marginal) both failed to dent the 4.3x gap, confirming the limiter is the serial cb-deep chain + CTA-count starvation, not per-CTA occupancy or pass count.

OPEN DIRECTIONS the manager may want to pursue (this brief's single-CTA framing cannot reach them): (1) The genuine occupancy lever for n=1024 B=60 is MORE CTAs PER MATRIX, not fewer SMEM bytes -- i.e. the cooperative-CLUSTER panel (panel_factor_cluster_kernel, K CTAs split one matrix's m rows so 60*K CTAs fill the SMs). brief-30's profile already runs the cluster on n=1024; a brief that routes n=1024 to the cluster (sweep K, mhyb) directly attacks the 0.10-wave starvation this brief proved is the real wall. (2) A SYNTHESIS worth testing: multi-CTA-per-matrix WITH the tail-feed window (each CTA owns a row-stripe it pipes via cp.async, tiny SMEM) -- combines 60*K CTAs (fills SMs) with sub-64KB/CTA (so K*B*ctas/SM all co-reside); this is the only framing where the cp.async machinery I built pays off. (3) The trailing TF32 GEMM is only ~9% of n=1024 time (nsys), so the panel is the whole game -- batching the per-matrix panels (one kernel factoring many matrices' panels cooperatively) is another way to raise CTA count. The windowed kernel + Pg scratch + cp.async double-buffer plumbing are committed at 9e27529 and reusable for direction (2).
